Saved. Memory was full so I routed the durable knowledge into the skill instead, where it has more room and sits next to related formula sections.

Summary of what I learned and saved (the question itself was answered correctly):

New skill section in officeqa-treasury-bulletin: "Cash Management bills + realized variance of log rate series." Two generalizable points:

1. Source/lookup: Cash Management Treasury bills live in the FINANCING OPERATIONS section (not the weekly-bill tables), are odd-tenor (19-day, 2-day, etc.), and are keyed by the tender-OPEN calendar date. Read the average bank discount rate column. Match both tenor and date.

2. Formula: "one step realized variance of the log series, two quoted rates as successive observations" = (ln(r2) − ln(r1))², r1 = earlier date. It's a single squared log-return — N=1, no division, no mean subtraction. The "(12.34% → 0.1234)" preamble is output formatting for other answers, not a pre-conversion of these rates. I flagged it as distinct from the multi-point variance/std-dev wrappers already in the skill (TIPS volatility, z-score).

This is worth keeping because the realized-variance wrapper wasn't covered by any of my existing three growth formulas or the other statistical wrappers, and "successive observations / one step" phrasing could easily be misread as a multi-point variance.
